title: Do Similarity Measures Measure Similarity? How User Activity Creates Phantom Correlation in Recommender Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.35765v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Item-item similarity is one of the oldest and most foundational signals in recommender systems: two items are assumed to be similar when the same users consume them. Despite the sparsity and scale of interaction data, the implicit assumption across the field is that item co-occurrence reflects genuine shared preference, capturing what users like together. In this paper, we demonstrate that a substantial fraction of observed item-item similarity is an artifact of variance in user activity rather than shared taste. Even if every user consumed items completely independently, differing only in their total consumption volume, standard similarity measures still detect strong associations between items. We term this phenomenon phantom correlation: spurious item association that emerges strictly from heterogeneous user activity in the complete absence of preference structure. translated_title: 相似性度量真的能度量相似性吗？用户活动如何在推荐系统中制造“幻影相关性”
translated_abstract: 物品间相似度是推荐系统中历史最悠久、最基础的信号之一：当相同用户消费两个物品时，这两个物品就被认为彼此相似。尽管交互数据稀疏且规模庞大，该领域普遍隐含的假设是，物品共现反映了真实的共同偏好，刻画了用户喜欢的物品组合。本文证明，所观测到的物品间相似度中有相当大一部分是用户活动量差异造成的伪象，而非共同品味所致。即使每个用户完全独立地消费物品，仅在总消费量上存在差异，标准的相似性度量依然能检测到物品之间强关联。我们将这一现象命名为“幻影相关性”：即在完全不存在偏好结构的情况下，仅由异质的用户活动引发的虚假物品关联。从最少的正式假设出发，我们表明……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出“幻影相关性”这一新现象，证明推荐系统中标准物品相似性度量即使在没有真实偏好结构的情况下，也会仅因用户活动量的异质性而检测出大量虚假的物品关联。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies "phantom correlation" in recommender systems, showing that standard item-item similarity measures detect strong spurious associations purely from heterogeneous user activity levels, even in the complete absence of genuine preference structure.
